item.title: Antarctica gained 695 billion tons in 2021-23 as tropical warmth drove heavy snowfall
item.description: Between 2021 and 2023, Antarctica experienced a notable gain in ice mass, primarily driven by exceptional snowfall in East Antarctica. This unusual occurrence, influenced by warmer tropical ocean temperatures, caused atmospheric disturbances that transported moisture southward. Although this gain temporarily countered ongoing ice loss in other regions, it does not signify a change in Antarctica's long-term trend of declining ice mass.

item.title: Meet Rachel Chen, 18, who won $100K for her breakthrough quantum math research using simple diagrams
item.description: Rachel Chen, an 18-year-old Los Angeles student, won $100,000 at the Regeneron Science Talent Search for expanding a 1997 mathematical idea involving Temperley-Lieb diagrams. Her research offers a visual way to describe complex quantum particle systems and spin representations, potentially helping researchers better understand connections between different quantum-mechanical states.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1973, Montana released a gall fly to control spotted knapweed; decades later...
item.description: Controlling invasive spotted knapweed biologically has initiated an unexpected ecological chain reaction. Gall flies, introduced as a control measure, have turned into a vital winter food source for deer mice, causing a surge in their populations and an uptick in hantavirus spread. Areas dense with knapweed report more infected mice than those with native grasslands.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: She bought a Maine island to stop clear-cutting; 90 years after Audubon opened its first camp there
item.description: Hog Island Audubon Camp marks an impressive ninety years of promoting environmental education and research. Located in Maine, this island was rescued from deforestation by environmentalists Millicent Todd Bingham and Mabel Loomis Todd. The camp is also the birthplace of Project Puffin, which successfully revitalized seabird numbers. Today, it remains a vital training ground for future scientists, educators, and artists, with its influence extending to bird conservation throughout North America.

item.title: Andrew Flintoff lists his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion, bought from Phil Neville in 2021
item.description: England cricket legend Andrew Flintoff has put his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion on the market, four years after his life-changing Top Gear car crash. Bought from former Manchester United star Phil Neville in 2021, the 10,000 sq ft luxury property features six bedrooms, six bathrooms, four floors, a pool, gym, cinema and games room.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: 5.3-magnitude quake hits Tibet as region reels from deadly flash floods
item.description: A magnitude 5.3 earthquake struck Tibet recently, following another tremor last week. Devastating flash floods hit the Tibet-Nepal border on August 26, causing widespread destruction. The disaster has raised concerns over the fragile Qinghai-Tibet Plateau environment. Rising temperatures and glacier melt are cited as contributing factors to the floods. Nepal's death toll from the floods has risen to 1,357 people.

item.title: Inside a $29M California mansion no one has ever lived in
item.description: A French-style manor in Rancho Santa Fe is now for sale at $29 million. This newly built home features antique materials and custom artisan craftsmanship throughout. The expansive residence includes a main house and a separate guest house on 3.66 acres. It boasts a zero-edge pool, gardens, and breathtaking views from its terraces. The manor comes fully furnished with art and antiques, ready for immediate occupancy.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Scientists seeded clouds over China’s Muz Taw Glacier; fresh snow cut ice loss by 14% to 17%
item.description: Scientists tested cloud seeding over China’s Muz Taw Glacier in 2018 to create artificial snowfall and slow ice loss. The experiment used silver iodide generators to encourage snow formation. Researchers found that fresh snow made the glacier surface brighter and reduced the amount of ice lost over a short period. However, they said the results are preliminary and need further testing.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Meet Anvith, Dubai student who watched his brother’s school commute and built a free carpool service
item.description: In a bid to tackle traffic congestion, a student from Dubai has launched a unique carpooling website that connects commuters with similar routes through sophisticated algorithmic matching. Community Carpool now boasts over a thousand registered users in Dubai, ensuring user privacy by discreetly matching individuals until they agree to share rides. Notably, a local property developer has embraced this platform for its workforce, facilitating its growth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Twin girls once given less than 10% chance of survival are now ready for their first day of school
item.description: Ruby and Scarlett were given less than a 10% chance of survival after being diagnosed with Twin-to-Twin Transfusion Syndrome at 16 weeks. Following high-risk surgery, premature birth and serious health complications, the twins spent 300 days in hospital. Now, their mother Hanna Brameld is celebrating as her daughters prepare for their first day of school.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: An 81-year-old US homeowner faced a $17,827.96 lien after a burst-pipe insurance claim was denied
item.description: Tyler Perry has made headlines with his philanthropic intervention for an elderly homeowner in Illinois. With her insurance company, Allstate, refusing to cover the damages from burst pipes, she faced the threat of foreclosure. Perry's willingness to pay off a significant property lien and provide additional financial support has saved her from losing her home and brightened her future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kentfield Home Hits Market: Long-held 1966 Laurel Grove house lists at $3.295m; charter club perk included
item.description: Now available on the market is a charming four-bedroom house in Kentfield, originally constructed in 1966. This midcentury gem has been tastefully renovated, featuring an expansive 2,784 square feet of living area set on a spacious lot. With modernized interiors and exclusive access to a local club, this well-established residence awaits its new owner after nearly sixty years of cherished memories.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: In 2023, an Australian cattle station sold for $40 million for a carbon project; three years later...
item.description: After a disappointing turn of events, Benmara Station, a prominent cattle property in Australia, was sold for A$26 million, significantly lower than its original price of A$40 million. This decline resulted from the cancellation of an ambitious environmental project related to carbon farming, emphasizing traditional pastoral values instead of its former carbon potential as regulatory challenges mounted.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Does AfD's big win in Germany signal a 'far right' uprising in Europe?
item.description: Many years ago, Otto von Bismarck observed that politics was “the art of the possible”. The modern European establishment appears to have inverted the Iron Chancellor’s maxim. Politics has increasingly become the art of explaining to voters why what they want is impossible, irresponsible, xenophobic, Islamophobic, nativist or, inevitably, far right. And made it impossible to vote for the so-called far-right party that’s actually willing to admit there’s a problem.
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: Panama City school left empty for years is getting a second life
item.description: The former Panama City Grammar School will undergo redevelopment into apartments and townhomes. City officials have cleared financial hurdles, waiving fines and providing a grant for the project. Developer Zachary Seymour will purchase the property and begin necessary structural repairs. The agreement mandates completion of critical repairs within one year to preserve the historic structure. Local leaders emphasize saving heritage, especially after Hurricane Michael's significant damage.
